new.title: Browse 1860s tin toys at the Antalya Toy Museum
new.desc: Opened in April 2011 in a restored warehouse at the Old Harbour, the museum is run by Antalya Metropolitan Municipality. Its cases hold well over a thousand toys from the 1860s onward.
new.tip: Free at the last listing; open 9:30-18:30, closed Mondays, so confirm before going. Pair it with a harbour stroll.
new.q: Antalya Oyuncak Müzesi, İskele Caddesi, Kaleiçi Yat Limanı, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Step into the Paleolithic shelter of Karain Cave
new.desc: Karain Cave lies on the Katran Mountains about 27 km north-west of Antalya and was lived in from the Paleolithic to the Iron Age. Finds from its excavations are shown in the Antalya Museum and a small museum beside the cave.
new.tip: Open daily, roughly 8-19 in summer and 8-17 in winter; allow an hour including the steps.
new.q: Karain Mağarası, Yağca Mahallesi, Döşemealtı, Antalya

new.title: Look down into Güver Canyon in Düzlerçamı
new.desc: A limestone canyon about 115 m deep and 2 km long, cut by the Karaman and Gürkayak streams in Düzlerçamı National Park. Viewpoints look out to the Gulf of Antalya and the Taurus.
new.tip: Free and open daily; turn left at the 15th km of the Antalya-Korkuteli road. Water in the canyon is seasonal, so spring is best.
new.q: Güver Uçurumu, Düzlerçamı Milli Parkı, Döşemealtı, Antalya

new.title: Walk the courtyard of the 13th-century Kırkgöz Han
new.desc: A Seljuk caravanserai built between 1237 and 1246 under Sultan Keykhusraw II on the Antalya-Konya caravan road, the second stop after Evdir. It was restored around 2009 and works as a tourist facility.
new.tip: Windowless outer walls and a classic courtyard plan are what to look for; a car is easiest.
new.q: Kırkgöz Hanı, Bıyıklı, Döşemealtı, Antalya

new.title: Seek out the ruined Seljuk caravanserai Evdir Han
new.desc: Built between 1210 and 1219 under İzzeddin Keykavus I near Yeşilbayır village, about 18 km north-west of Antalya. It is heavily ruined, though restoration work took place in the 2010s.
new.tip: Combine it with Karain Cave, a few kilometres away.
new.q: Evdir Han, Yeşilbayır, Döşemealtı, Antalya

new.title: Visit Atatürk House, where he stayed in 1930 and 1935
new.desc: A house in central Antalya, demolished in 1984, rebuilt and reopened as the Atatürk House and Museum in 1986. It records Atatürk's visits to the city in 1930 and 1935.
new.tip: Check opening days before you go; it is a short visit of about 30 minutes.
new.q: Antalya Atatürk Evi Müzesi, Haşim İşcan Mahallesi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Wander Ormana's dry-stone button houses
new.desc: A mountain village in İbradı at about 950 m, named one of the UN Tourism Best Tourism Villages in 2024. Its düğmeli (button) houses use dry-stacked stone with cedar timber, some said to be 300 years old.
new.tip: About 60 km from Manavgat and 2 to 2.5 hours from Antalya by car; village tea houses serve local food.
new.q: Ormana Köyü, İbradı, Antalya

new.title: Cool off at Uçansu Waterfall in the Alara valley
new.desc: A waterfall of about 50 m on the Alara stream near Kayabükü village in Gündoğmuş, split into three arms and protected as a natural site since 1992. Snowmelt feeds it, so it flows strongest from March to August.
new.tip: About 25 km from Gündoğmuş; small restaurants and pensions stand nearby. Check water levels first as it can run low.
new.q: Uçansu Şelalesi, Kayabükü, Gündoğmuş, Antalya

new.title: Stroll restored buttoned houses in Sarıhacılar, Akseki
new.desc: A neighbourhood of Akseki said to be around 800 years old, with restored Ottoman-style düğmeli houses and ties to the old Silk Road. Restoration was supported by the Antalya governorship.
new.tip: Akseki is about 150 km from Antalya at 1,100 m; go in spring or summer.
new.q: Sarıhacılar Mahallesi, Akseki, Antalya

new.title: Share fish meze at Balıkçı Meyhanesi in Kaleiçi
new.desc: A seafood meyhane in a stone townhouse in the old town, open since 1994 and known for fish meze. Reviewers single out the octopus and the seafood platter.
new.tip: Busy at weekends, with live music reported on Friday and Saturday nights; book ahead.
new.q: Balıkçı Meyhanesi, Hesapçı Sokak, Kaleiçi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Eat fresh fish to live music at Ayar Meyhanesi
new.desc: A Kaleiçi meyhane on Hesapçı Sokak with a terrace and small pool, praised for fresh fish and evening live music.
new.tip: Fish is on the pricey side; ask the price per kilo before you order.
new.q: Ayar Meyhanesi, Hesapçı Sokak 59, Kaleiçi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Dine to live music at Yemenli Meyhanesi
new.desc: A meyhane in a historic stone building in Kaleiçi, with tables spilling into the street and live music over dinner. Guides also name it for traditional Antalya dishes.
new.tip: Come after 8 pm for the music and book at weekends.
new.q: Yemenli Meyhanesi, Kaleiçi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Start the day with börek at Börekçi Tevfik
new.desc: A breakfast and börek spot in the Ay İşhanı on Peker Caddesi, Muratpaşa, listed among Antalya breakfast places.
new.tip: Go early for fresh börek with tea.
new.q: Börekçi Tevfik, Peker Caddesi, Sinan Mahallesi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Have a village breakfast at Çakırlar Köy Kahvaltısı
new.desc: A Konyaaltı restaurant serving köy kahvaltısı, a spread of cheeses, olives, eggs, jams and fresh bread, named among the best breakfasts in Antalya.
new.tip: Weekend mornings fill up; arrive before 10.
new.q: Çakırlar Köy Kahvaltısı, Sosyete Pazarı, Akdamlar, Çakırlar, Konyaaltı, Antalya

new.title: Order grilled sea bass at Lara Balıkevi
new.desc: A seafood restaurant on Lara Caddesi, open since 2002 and reputed for some of the best fish in Antalya.
new.tip: Ask for the catch of the day and have it grilled.
new.q: Lara Balıkevi, Lara Caddesi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Queue for Giliğ dondurma in Konyaaltı
new.desc: An ice-cream shop that began on a three-wheeled trolley in Korkuteli and is now cited as the best ice cream in town, with long queues.
new.tip: Try the burnt-milk (yanık) flavour, an Antalya speciality.
new.q: Giliğ Dondurma, Konyaaltı, Antalya

new.title: Scoop dondurma at Dondurma Dükkanı
new.desc: Listed as one of the most popular ice-cream shops in Antalya.
new.tip: A good stop after a Kaleiçi walk.
new.q: Dondurma Dükkanı, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Pull Maraş-style ice cream at Çavuşoğlu Dondurma
new.desc: A shop serving stretchy Kahramanmaraş-style ice cream, reviewed as delicious and affordable.
new.tip: Eat it with a knife and fork as in Maraş if the staff offer.
new.q: Çavuşoğlu Dondurma, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Eat at the old kebab house Topçu Kebap Salonu
new.desc: Named in guides as an old local kebab house in Antalya.
new.tip: Order the Adana or şiş and pair it with şalgam.
new.q: Topçu Kebap Salonu, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Try 60 mushroom dishes at Mantar Evi in Korkuteli
new.desc: Korkuteli grows about 54 percent of Turkey's mushrooms, and Mantar Evi builds its menu around them with about 60 dishes, plus regional food.
new.tip: Reviewers recommend the mushroom döner; also try Korkuteli yanık dondurma.
new.q: Mantar Evi, Antalya Yolu No:11/A, Tatköy, Korkuteli, Antalya

new.title: Eat fresh local dishes at Monte Kemer
new.desc: A relaxed Kemer restaurant that guides credit with affordable fresh local food.
new.tip: Cheaper than the marina front.
new.q: Monte Restaurant, Merkez, Kemer, Antalya

new.title: Eat trout from the farm at Ulupınar Havuzbaşı
new.desc: A Kemer restaurant serving fresh fish from a working trout farm.
new.tip: Fish is caught to order, so allow time.
new.q: Ulupınar Havuzbaşı Restaurant, Ulupınar, Kemer, Antalya

new.title: Walk the cliff-top Atatürk Park to Konyaaltı
new.desc: A cliff-top park strip along Konyaaltı Caddesi, reopened in its present form in 2006, between Kaleiçi and Konyaaltı Beach near the Cam Piramit. The wider Atatürk Kültür Parkı has a boating lake and café.
new.tip: About 2 km of easy walking from the Clock Tower; the nostalgic tram runs the route back.
new.q: Atatürk Parkı, Konyaaltı Caddesi, Muratpaşa, Antalya

new.title: Learn nomad culture at Yörük Park in Kemer
new.desc: A themed open-air park near central Kemer on the Küçükburun peninsula showing traditional Yörük nomadic life, with folk music and local food.
new.tip: Walkable from Kemer centre.
new.q: Yörük Parkı, Küçükburun, Kemer, Antalya

new.title: Ski and swim in one day at Saklıkent
new.desc: A ski centre on Bakırlı Mountain in the Beydağları, about 45 to 50 km from Antalya, with a season of roughly December to April, a chairlift and a T-bar.
new.tip: Bus line 500 takes about an hour from the city; check snow reports first.
new.q: Saklıkent Kayak Merkezi, Bakırlı Dağı, Kemer, Antalya

new.title: Swim at the public beach of Çamyuva
new.desc: A coast about 7 km from Kemer between Kemer and Tekirova, with about 3 km of shoreline and a public beach for day visitors beside hotel beaches.
new.tip: Dolmuş from Kemer; bring shade in midsummer.
new.q: Çamyuva Plajı, Çamyuva, Kemer, Antalya

new.title: Swim in calm water at Beldibi Beach Park
new.desc: Beldibi is chosen by travellers who want calm water and fewer crowds; Beldibi Beach Park is a green space by the shore.
new.tip: Quieter outside July and August.
new.q: Beldibi Plaj Parkı, Beldibi, Kemer, Antalya

new.title: Hike the Alara stream trail from Narağacı to the falls
new.desc: A walking route of about 10 km along the Alara stream in Gündoğmuş, from Narağacı to Ortakonuş, ending at Uçansu waterfall. The Alara is also used for rafting.
new.tip: Cool in summer; ask locally about water levels.
new.q: Narağacı, Gündoğmuş, Antalya
